title: Complete fmonero wallet workflows and Omarchy product integration
description:
# fmonero: complete wallet workflows and intuitive desktop integration

Requested 2026-10-13 by Oliver. Implement the daily-use improvements and the advanced GUI features in this round. Use the installed jsm-managed br/bv, NTM/vibing, UX/UI, Rust optimization and gauntlet skills. Plan and refine the dependency graph before coding. Keep the team small and centralize builds.

## Product outcome

A person can open, create or restore a wallet, create labeled receiving subaddresses and payment requests, see received/confirmed/spendable state, safely prepare/send/sweep payments, manage contacts/accounts, inspect useful live logs, and use advanced watch-only, cold-signing, hardware, signing and proof tools without memorizing command-line management. The app remains on demand and the Omarchy widget remains a thin useful companion.

## Scope and boundaries

1. Local checksum validation: verify Keccak-256 after Base58 decoding for every supported address form/network; reject a changed checksum while offline; retain Monero's authoritative validation before sending. No accidental SHA3 substitution.
2. Remote transport: explicit auto/required/disabled TLS policy, CA/fingerprint options and SOCKS proxy; apply identically at startup and set_daemon. Preserve old config migration; HTTPS means required TLS; certificate failure cannot silently fall back.
3. Privacy: one persisted setting shared by TUI/widget; mask amounts, addresses, wallet names, notes, payment details and notification contents, with deliberate reveal for payment review. No hidden destination at final confirmation.
4. Receive/requests: new labeled subaddress, selected/copy/QR after creation; exact integer-amount monero: URI generation/parsing, reject unknown/unsafe parameters; review pasted requests before preparing payments; track receiving/confirmed/spendable through real wallet observations.
5. Restore: real deterministic-seed restoration with name, masked seed/password, height or date guidance, no overwrites, backend startup/node setup, clear progress/cancel/error states and discoverable opening of the restored wallet. Input protection is a hard requirement, not a stub or merely an external documentation link.
6. Logs: bounded live wallet/node/service/application sources; follow/pause/search, source labels, secret redaction, resource limits, remote-mode usefulness and no service starts from log viewing.
7. Send/sweep: TUI send-all and normal multi-transaction preparation where needed; exact cumulative fees/amounts, persisted pending state, successful partial relay handling, no ambiguous retry; optional fee ceiling available consistently.
8. Contacts/accounts: create/list/rename/select accounts and add/edit/remove recipients through the wallet engine; confirmation for destructive contact edits and unambiguous @ lookup.
9. Maintenance: deliberate rescan (spent/full as appropriate), password change and safe guided backup/recovery; no competing wallet-file writers. File artifacts are explicit and owner-only, never overwrite silently.
10. Convenience: redacted opt-in incoming-payment notifications while the wallet service is active; deterministic exact CSV/JSON history export to an explicit destination.
11. View-only: create/open view-only wallets, clearly show incoming-only versus spendable evidence; key-image import/export with explicit inputs and correct trust requirements.
12. Offline transactions: prepare unsigned artifacts, describe and review recipient/amount/fee, sign with the offline wallet, then explicitly submit signed artifacts. Never treat file presence or a timeout as broadcast success.
13. Hardware: integrate Monero's supported device workflow (Ledger/Trezor); actual creation/opening/signing delegated to the engine. Present connectivity/locked-device failures clearly. Physical device qualification is a separately recorded limitation when no device is available.
14. Signing/proofs: sign and verify messages, create/check transaction proofs, spend proofs and reserve proofs through typed supported backend calls. Keep proofs/signatures distinct from private keys.
15. UI: consistent mnemonic labels, semantic colors, keyboard/mouse parity, visible controls and focus, editable forms, narrow-terminal fallback, coherent grouping of ordinary versus advanced tools. Retain existing working navigation aliases where unambiguous.
16. Omarchy: extend the installed oliver.monero plugin with privacy, Receive/New address, requests/log/tool shortcuts and notifications; correct desktop branding; install idempotently; full shutdown and idle behavior remain correct.
17. Performance/gauntlet: bounded resource build helper, baseline latency/allocation/syscall evidence before tuning; focused conformance, round-trip, negative/fault and real isolated Monero checks, visual/mouse tests, workspace checks, fresh review, installation and artifact cleanup. Do not claim real funded payment or device acceptance from mocks.

## Delivery waves

- Foundation wave: core checksum/transport/API groundwork and UI mnemonic/color/mouse foundation in disjoint domains. No agent builds.
- Wallet wave: backend workflows and CLI contracts, then UI forms consuming those typed APIs. Central compile and focused regression tests unblock dependents.
- Integration wave: receiving, advanced workflows, logs, widget and installer. Preserve existing owner sessions and service configuration unless the feature installation requires a deliberate update.
- Qualification wave: one builder, isolated scratch backend tests, actual UI interaction/captures, profile and bounded optimizations, feature-scope gauntlet, two fresh review passes, install and cleanup.

The br issues are the execution source of truth. Each issue contains its positive behavior, failure cases, owned files, tests, dependencies and evidence limits. Closure is by the orchestrator after central verification, not by an implementing agent.
acceptance_criteria: Requested daily-use and advanced workflows are implemented, centrally tested and installed; resource usage remains bounded; funded-payment and hardware evidence limits are explicit.

title: Offline checksum validation for every supported address
description:
Owner-authorized scope: docs/IMPLEMENTATION.md and AGENTS.md. Use the existing Monero engine, typed bounded calls, integer piconero, explicit review and payment locks. Protect seeds/passwords/private keys from arguments, environment, ordinary output, logging, clipboard, app state, caches, checked-in fixtures and Debug. Do not touch owner wallets or real units in tests. Implement real code and meaningful positive/negative tests; no shipped stubs. Agents do not build or self-close; the orchestrator verifies centrally, then closes with evidence. Preserve the working launch fix and on-demand lifecycle.

## Implementation
Decode Monero Base58 and verify Keccak-256 checksum for standard, subaddress and integrated addresses on mainnet/stagenet/testnet. Keep RPC validation authoritative before payment. Update TUI live validation and offline CLI semantics through the existing parser, preserving the refusal order. Owned: address.rs, Cargo manifests, address fixtures/tests.

## Evidence
Cite exact tests and paths in the handoff. The orchestrator closes after a central verified wave.

## Core review: integration and failure behavior (2026-10-13)
Preserve address::parse as the CLI/TUI entry point and its existing refusal order. Cover all nine network/form combinations with independent public Monero vectors, canonical Base58 decoding and exact payload lengths; do not manufacture correctness using the new encoder alone. Core updates core tests; root owns any test-server/fixture or scripts/check.sh changes outside crates/fmonero-core. The manifest freeze is superseded, but only add a reviewed Keccak implementation, not a replacement wallet engine.

Core owns crates/fmonero-core/** and workspace manifests/lockfile only. Root owns fixture-server, CLI, shared scripts/docs and central verification; UI owns TUI. Proposed boundary contract: /tmp/fmonero-core-review.md (review only; agree APIs before source edits). All isolated runs must set FMONERO_STATE_DIR, FMONERO_CONFIG_DIR, FMONERO_CACHE_DIR, XDG_DATA_HOME, FMONERO_SYSTEMD_USER_DIR, FMONERO_SYSTEMCTL_FIXTURE and FMONERO_NODES_URL together. Central evidence must separately label source/unit/mock, isolated Monero 0.18.5.3, funded-payment and physical-device coverage; no agent runs builds/tests or closes this issue.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Valid upstream public vectors parse on all networks/forms; a one-character checksum mutation fails offline.
- [x] Malformed/overflow Base58 blocks and invalid network prefixes remain rejected.
- [x] No SHA3 substitution; current mock fixtures retain meaningful real checksum-valid addresses.
- [x] Positive vectors cover standard/subaddress/integrated addresses on mainnet/testnet/stagenet; checksum-invalid, wrong-network, noncanonical block, invalid-length and overflow cases fail without RPC.
- [x] A checksum-valid address is still checked by Monero before payment; local validation never claims ownership, spendability or supported-wallet capability.
close_reason: Software qualified by workspace490, fullCLI906, actualPTY207, checksum/URI corpus, nativeMonero23, TLS/proxy18 and real untrusted/trustedTLS boundary checks. Evidence: docs/QUALIFICATION.md and .beads/evidence/software-qualified.json. Physical/funded/live-unlocked-desktop acceptance remains separate.

title: Unsigned, signed and submitted offline transaction workflows
description:

## Implementation
Implement prepare/save unsigned transaction, describe/review, offline signing and explicit signed-file submission. Integrate payment guards, content validation, no overwrites and persistent uncertainty. Typed explicit commands only, not generic RPC escape hatch. Owned: advanced transaction helpers and rpc/send tests.

## Evidence
Cite exact tests and paths in the handoff. The orchestrator closes after a central verified wave.

## Core review: integration and failure behavior (2026-10-13)
Keep prepare-unsigned, synchronize outputs/key images, describe, review, sign, export and submit as separate typed operations with Monero performing parsing/signing. Offline signing must run with auto-refresh/network contact disabled, not reuse an online wallet service and call it offline. Monero 0.18.5.3 describe_transfer takes unsigned or multisig txsets and refuses watch-only/HW wallets; it has no signed_txset input. submit_transfer commits the signed set internally, and an error can follow a partial commit. Therefore agree a concrete backend-backed signed-artifact review route with root before implementation (e.g. a bounded Monero CLI acceptance adapter with exclusive wallet ownership); never trust a user-editable sidecar or a file hash alone as recipient/amount proof. Bind review to exact immutable bytes, wallet/network, every recipient/change/fee and expected txids where known. Persist uncertainty before dispatch, including when expected txids are not yet available; do not call submit for inspection or auto-retry a failed submission.

Core owns crates/fmonero-core/** and workspace manifests/lockfile only. Root owns fixture-server, CLI, shared scripts/docs and central verification; UI owns TUI. Proposed boundary contract: /tmp/fmonero-core-review.md (review only; agree APIs before source edits). All isolated runs must set FMONERO_STATE_DIR, FMONERO_CONFIG_DIR, FMONERO_CACHE_DIR, XDG_DATA_HOME, FMONERO_SYSTEMD_USER_DIR, FMONERO_SYSTEMCTL_FIXTURE and FMONERO_NODES_URL together. Central evidence must separately label source/unit/mock, isolated Monero 0.18.5.3, funded-payment and physical-device coverage; no agent runs builds/tests or closes this issue.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Unsigned and signed artifacts have real backend paths, exact recipient/amount/fee review and private atomic files.
- [x] Submission requires explicit confirmation and protects pending/ambiguous outcomes without auto-retry.
- [x] Malformed/untrusted/mismatched files fail before relay; no funded broadcasts are run by development tests.
- [x] A positive unsigned-describe-sign-export path uses Monero on isolated scratch wallets, verifies exact recipients/change/fees and never broadcasts; lack of inputs is not counted as successful signing evidence.
- [x] The signed submission review is derived from Monero for the exact loaded bytes, not filename/extension/sidecar; replacing an artifact after review cannot change what is signed/submitted.
- [x] One lock guards signed submit, explicit typed-send/--yes confirmation follows full review, and any partial-commit error/timeout persists uncertainty that blocks later payments without retry.
- [x] Offline steps prove no daemon contact; malformed, wrong-wallet/network/kind and excessive artifacts fail before signing/relay; software/mock evidence remains separate from unrun funded broadcast evidence.

## Evidence

## Core review: integration and failure behavior (2026-10-13)
Use small typed message and proof requests rather than arbitrary RPC method/JSON dispatch. Pin sign/verify and get/check_tx_proof, get/check_spend_proof, get/check_reserve_proof fields to Monero 0.18.5.3; distinguish proof kind, network/address/account, exact message bytes and optional amount/all choice. Respect full/view-only/device capability and each online/trusted-node prerequisite. Do not fetch transaction secret keys merely to create a proof when the backend proof call suffices. Results must separate valid=false from unavailable/error and report amounts in piconero without asserting more than that proof establishes. Proof strings are shareable evidence of sensitive financial facts, not private wallet keys; privacy masks automatic previews and sharing/export is deliberate.
